questions.q: The thyroid gland descends from the tongue starting at:
questions.exp: Embryology: foramen caecum (posterior 1/3rd tongue) → thyroglossal tract → thyroid gland; tract obliterates. (Book p102)

questions.q: The foramen caecum lies at the junction of:
questions.exp: Foramen caecum between anterior 2/3rd and posterior 1/3rd of tongue. (Book p102)

questions.q: Lingual thyroid is:
opts: Undescended thyroid tissue just below the tongue
questions.exp: Lingual thyroid: undescended thyroid tissue; site just below the tongue. (Book p102)

questions.q: On clinical examination of lingual thyroid, the swelling causes:
questions.exp: C/F: swelling → tongue lifted up. (Book p102)

questions.q: Before excising a lingual thyroid, USG neck is done to:
opts: Check for normal thyroid tissue in the neck
questions.exp: Ix: FNAC shows thyroid tissue; USG neck before Sx to check for normal thyroid tissue. (Book p102)

questions.q: After excision of a lingual thyroid that was the only thyroid tissue, the patient needs:
questions.exp: Mx: excision + thyroxine supplementation if it is the only thyroid tissue. (Book p102)

questions.q: A thyroglossal cyst is due to:
questions.exp: Etiology: persistent thyroglossal tract. (Book p102)

questions.q: The most common site of a thyroglossal cyst is:
questions.exp: Site: subhyoid (m/c). (Book p102)

questions.q: A thyroglossal cyst presents as a midline neck swelling that moves with:
questions.exp: Midline neck swelling: moves with deglutition & protrusion of tongue. (Book p102)

questions.q: The Sistrunk procedure removes:
opts: Cyst + part of hyoid bone + tract till base of tongue
questions.exp: Sistrunk: removal of cyst + part of hyoid bone + tract till base of tongue. (Book p102)

questions.q: Incision & drainage of a thyroglossal cyst is never done because it leads to:
questions.exp: Incision & drainage → thyroglossal fistula: NEVER done. (Book p102)

questions.q: Complications of a thyroglossal cyst include thyroglossal fistula and:
questions.exp: Complications: 1. Thyroglossal fistula (mx: Sistrunk); 2. Papillary thyroid carcinoma in long standing cases. (Book p102)

questions.q: An inflamed thyroglossal cyst can lead to:
questions.exp: Inflamed thyroglossal cyst can lead to fistula. (Book p103)

questions.q: Thyroglossal vs branchial fistula: thyroglossal is midline and always acquired; branchial fistula lies:
questions.exp: Branchial fistula: lower 1/3rd along sternocleidomastoid; congenital/acquired (thyroglossal: midline, always acquired). (Book p103)

questions.q: Clinical features of hyperthyroidism include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Features: thin irritable patient, weight loss DESPITE good appetite, tachycardia, diarrhoea, tremors, heat intolerance, oligomenorrhea. (Book p103)

questions.q: The most common cause of hyperthyroidism with diffuse ↑ uptake on thyroid scan is:
questions.exp: Graves' disease: m/c; diffuse ↑ uptake. (Book p103)

questions.q: Solitary toxic nodule/Plummer's disease shows on thyroid scan:
questions.exp: Solitary toxic nodule/Plummer's: ↑ single hot nodule. (Book p103)

questions.q: Toxic nodular goitre shows on scan:
questions.exp: Toxic nodular goitre: ↑ multiple hot nodules. (Book p103)

questions.q: Factitious hyperthyroidism (↑ exogenous intake) shows on thyroid scan:
questions.exp: Factitious hyperthyroidism: ↓ uptake (so does struma ovarii - ectopic thyroid in ovary). (Book p103)

questions.q: Jod-Basedow phenomenon is:
questions.exp: Jod-Basedow phenomenon: I2 induced hyperthyroidism (↑ uptake). (Book p103)

questions.q: A TSH secreting pituitary adenoma causes hyperthyroidism with:
questions.exp: TSH secreting pituitary adenoma: ↑ TSH, ↑ uptake. (Book p103)

questions.q: Struma ovarii is:
opts: Ectopic thyroid tissue in ovary (↓ neck uptake)
questions.exp: Struma ovarii: ectopic thyroid tissue in ovary; neck scan ↓. (Book p103)

questions.q: The antithyroid drugs are:
questions.exp: Drugs only: 1. PTU; 2. carbimazole. (Book p103)

questions.q: Mechanism of PTU/carbimazole includes:
opts: (-) thyroid peroxidase enzyme and blocking T4 → T3
questions.exp: Mechanism: (-) thyroid peroxidase enzyme; T4 →(-) T3 (PTU also blocks peripheral conversion). (Book p103)

questions.q: The antithyroid drug safe in 1st trimester of pregnancy & lactation is:
questions.exp: PTU safe in 1st trimester of pregnancy & lactation. (Book p103)

questions.q: The important side effect of antithyroid drugs and its 1st sign are:
questions.exp: S/E: agranulocytosis; 1st sign: sore throat. (Book p103)

questions.q: Radioiodine ablation for hyperthyroidism uses I-131 which:
opts: Acts via β rays; t½ 7-8 days
Acts via α rays; t½ 7 days
Acts via γ rays; t½ 8 days
Acts via β rays; t½ 70 days
questions.exp: RIA: I131 acts via β rays; t½ 7-8 days. (Book p104)

questions.q: Antithyroid drugs are started how many weeks before surgery?
questions.exp: Start antithyroid drugs 6-8 wks before Sx. (Book p104)

questions.q: The long acting β blocker given prior to thyroid surgery is:
questions.exp: Nadolol OD (long acting β blocker) prior to Sx. (Book p104)

questions.q: Nadolol is continued for 7 days post Sx because:
opts: Half life of T3 is 7 days
Half life of T4 is 7 days
questions.exp: Continue 7 days post Sx (half life of T3: 7 days); advantage ↑ sympathetic outflow control; last dose evening before Sx. (Book p104)

questions.q: The last dose of β blocker before thyroid surgery is given:
questions.exp: Last dose: evening before Sx. (Book p104)

questions.q: Drugs before thyroid surgery aim to:
questions.exp: Drugs: to achieve euthyroid state (prevent thyroid storm). (Book p104)

questions.q: Thyroid storm is:
questions.exp: Thyroid storm: uncontrolled thyrotoxicosis. (Book p104)

questions.q: The most common etiology of thyroid storm is:
questions.exp: Etiology: inadequately prepared patient (m/c); URTI; interventions (FNAC); Sx trauma; anaesthetic agents. (Book p104)

questions.q: The leading cause of death in thyroid storm is:
questions.exp: Features: dehydration, hyperthermia, HTN crisis, palpitations → arrhythmia (leading cause of death). (Book p104)

questions.q: Aggressive IV fluid therapy in thyroid storm prevents dehydration and:
questions.exp: Aggressive IV fluids: prevent dehydration & acute tubular necrosis. (Book p104)

questions.q: Hyperthermia in thyroid storm is managed with:
questions.exp: Hyperthermia: cold fluids/packs. (Book p104)

questions.q: The large-dose β blocker used in thyroid storm is:
questions.exp: Mx: IV steroid & antibiotics; large dose β blockers (propranolol); PTU/carbimazole. (Book p104)

questions.q: Which drug must be AVOIDED in thyroid storm as it worsens the condition?
questions.exp: Avoid aspirin (worsens the condition). (Book p104)

questions.q: Graves' disease is:
opts: Autoimmune condition (female > male), m/c cause of hyperthyroidism
questions.exp: Autoimmune (female > male); m/c cause of hyperthyroidism. (Book p104)

questions.q: The etiology of Graves' disease is:
questions.exp: TRAb: stimulating antibodies (earlier called LATS: long acting thyroid stimulating antibodies). (Book p104)

questions.q: The dermopathy of Graves' disease is:
questions.exp: Dermopathy: pretibial myxedema. (Book p104)

questions.q: Graves' disease is associated with:
questions.exp: Associations: pernicious anemia; myasthenia gravis. (Book p105)

questions.q: Thyroid acropachy refers to:
questions.exp: Thyroid acropachy: subperiosteal bone formation. (Book p105)

questions.q: Exophthalmos in Graves' shows:
questions.exp: Exophthalmos: upper sclera is visible. (Book p105)

questions.q: Von Graefe's sign and Dalrymple's sign (lid lag & lid retraction) are due to:
questions.exp: Von Graefe (lid lag) & Dalrymple (lid retraction): d/t spasm of Muller muscle. (Book p105)

questions.q: Muller's muscle is the:
questions.exp: Muller's muscle → autonomic component of LPS. (Book p105)

questions.q: Joffroy's sign is:
opts: Absence of forehead wrinkling when patient looks up
questions.exp: Joffroy's sign: absence of forehead wrinkling when patient looks up. (Book p105)

questions.q: Moebius sign (sign of severe toxicity) is:
questions.exp: Moebius sign (severe toxicity): loss of accommodation reflex. (Book p105)

questions.q: Stellwag sign (sign of mild toxicity) is:
questions.exp: Stellwag sign (mild toxicity): infrequent blinking/staring look. (Book p105)

questions.q: Dx of Graves' is based on:
questions.exp: Dx based on C/F + autoantibody levels; diffuse enlargement + hyperthyroid features + eye signs. (Book p105)

questions.q: HPE of Graves' disease shows:
opts: Scalloping of colloid with tall columnar cells
questions.exp: HPE: scalloping of colloid; tall columnar cells. (Book p105)

questions.q: A child with Graves' disease is treated with:
questions.exp: Child: drugs only. (Book p105)

questions.q: A pregnant patient with Graves' is treated with:
questions.exp: Pregnant: drugs only - PTU. (Book p105)

questions.q: An adult Graves' patient WITHOUT goitre is managed with:
questions.exp: Adult without goitre: drugs → RIA; with goitre: drugs → Sx. (Book p105)

questions.q: An elderly Graves' patient with comorbidities is managed with:
questions.exp: Elderly with comorbidities: drugs → RIA. (Book p105)

questions.q: Graves' with extensive eye signs is treated with drugs → Sx because:
questions.exp: With extensive eye signs: drugs → Sx; RIA is C/I (worsens eye signs). (Book p105)

questions.q: The preferred surgical option in Graves' is:
questions.exp: Sx: total thyroidectomy > subtotal/near total thyroidectomy. (Book p105)

questions.q: Plummer's disease/toxic nodular goitre has female:male ratio and rank among hyperthyroidism causes of:
questions.exp: Plummer's: female:male 5:1; 2nd m/c cause of hyperthyroidism. (Book p106)

questions.q: Thyroid scan in Plummer's disease/toxic nodular goitre shows:
questions.exp: Scan: multiple hot & cold nodules. (Book p106)

questions.q: Mx of Plummer's disease/toxic nodular goitre is:
questions.exp: Mx: drugs → total thyroidectomy. (Book p106)

questions.q: A solitary toxic nodule (5th decade, female > male) shows on scan and is treated with:
questions.exp: Solitary toxic nodule: single hot nodule; mx drugs → RIA. (Book p106)

questions.q: The most common cause of hypothyroidism overall is:
questions.exp: Iodine deficiency: m/c overall; Hashimoto: m/c in west. (Book p106)

questions.q: The most common cause of hypothyroidism in the west is:
questions.exp: Hashimoto thyroiditis: m/c in west. (Book p106)

questions.q: Wolff-Chaikoff phenomenon is:
questions.exp: Wolff-Chaikoff: iodine induced hypothyroidism (Jod-Basedow is the hyper counterpart). (Book p106)

questions.q: Sheehan syndrome is:
questions.exp: Sheehan syndrome: post partum pituitary apoplexy. (Book p106)

questions.q: Dyshormonogenesis refers to:
questions.exp: Dyshormonogenesis: TPO enzyme deficiency. (Book p106)

questions.q: Refetoff syndrome is:
opts: Elderly patients with end organ resistance to T4
questions.exp: Refetoff syndrome: elderly patients with end organ resistance to T4. (Book p106)

questions.q: A non-functioning pituitary adenoma causes hypothyroidism with ↓ TSH; this is:
questions.exp: Non functioning pituitary adenoma: ↓ TSH (exception). (Book p106)

questions.q: Clinical features of hypothyroidism include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Features: dull lethargic, alopecia, bradycardia, constipation, weight GAIN, cold intolerance, menorrhagia. (Book p106)

questions.q: Hashimoto's (lymphocytic) thyroiditis incidence is:
opts: Autoimmune, female > male, strong hereditary component
questions.exp: Autoimmune: female > male; strong hereditary component. (Book p106)

questions.q: Hashimoto's is associated with HLA:
questions.exp: A/w: HLA DR3/B8; Down's & Turner's syndromes. (Book p106)

questions.q: Hashimoto's is associated with which chromosomal syndromes?
questions.exp: Down's & Turner's syndromes. (Book p106)

questions.q: Autoantibodies in Hashimoto's are against:
questions.exp: Autoantibodies against thyroid receptors (blocking receptors), TPO enzyme, thyroglobulin. (Book p107)

questions.q: The brief early hyperthyroid phase of Hashimoto's is called:
questions.exp: Stored hormones released → hashitoxicosis (↑ T3, T4 briefly) then prolonged hypothyroidism. (Book p107)

questions.q: Long standing Hashimoto's cases can develop which cancers (m/c first)?
questions.exp: Long standing cases: lymphoma (m/c cancer), FTC, PTC. (Book p107)

questions.q: FNAC in Hashimoto's shows:
questions.exp: Ix: autoantibody levels; FNAC lymphocyte infiltration + Hurthle cells. (Book p107)

questions.q: Mx of Hashimoto's is:
opts: Low dose thyroxine gradually titrated till TSH becomes normal; total thyroidectomy if goitre (+)
questions.exp: Low dose thyroxine gradually titrated till TSH normal; if goitre (+) → total thyroidectomy. (Book p107)

questions.q: Subacute thyroiditis is also called:
questions.exp: De Quervain/viral/granulomatous thyroiditis; associated with HLA B35. (Book p108)

questions.q: The sentinel event for subacute thyroiditis is:
questions.exp: Sentinel event: URTI (viral); after 4-6 weeks lymphocytic infiltration. (Book p108)

questions.q: The clinical course of subacute thyroiditis is:
questions.exp: Spike of hyperthyroidism → hypothyroidism → euthyroid (self limiting); follicles regenerate in 2-3 months. (Book p108)

questions.q: Subacute thyroiditis classically presents with painful neck enlargement and:
questions.exp: Painful neck enlargement; ↑ ESR. (Book p108)

questions.q: Mx of subacute thyroiditis is:
questions.exp: Mx: symptomatic; steroids. (Book p108)

questions.q: Post-partum thyroiditis is seen in what timeframe and frequency?
questions.exp: Seen in 2-12 months post partum (in 10%). (Book p108)

questions.q: The etiology of post-partum thyroiditis is:
questions.exp: Etiology: autoimmune thyroiditis (2nd m/c cause); anti TPO antibodies (+); 10 fold risk of Hashimoto's. (Book p108)

questions.q: Mx of post-partum thyroiditis is:
questions.exp: Mx: correction of hypothyroidism; features same as Hashimoto. (Book p108)

questions.q: Riedel's/fibrosing thyroiditis associations include:
questions.exp: Associations: IgG4; Peyronie's disease; Dupuytren's contracture. (Book p108)

questions.q: Fibrosis within the gland in Riedel's causes:
questions.exp: Within gland → painless enlargement → woody hard. (Book p108)

questions.q: Fibrosis in the vicinity of the gland causes pressure symptoms:
questions.exp: In vicinity → pressure symptoms: RLN hoarseness; trachea stridor. (Book p108)

questions.q: The important D/D of Riedel's thyroiditis is:
questions.exp: D/D: anaplastic cancer. (Book p109)

questions.q: Ix and Mx of Riedel's thyroiditis are:
opts: USG guided core biopsy; steroids + tamoxifen
questions.exp: Ix: USG guided core biopsy; mx: steroids, tamoxifen. (Book p109)

questions.q: Summary: painful neck swelling with URTI history and spontaneous recovery is:
questions.exp: Subacute: H/o URTI, painful, hyper→hypo→spontaneous recovery; Hashimoto painless prolonged hypo; Riedel painless hard gland. (Book p109)

questions.q: Etiology of diffuse goitre includes all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Diffuse goitre: iodine deficiency, pregnancy & puberty (demand states), Hashimoto's, Graves'. (Book p109)

questions.q: Untreated diffuse goitre progresses to MNG due to:
questions.exp: Untreated diffuse goitre → MNG (d/t variable TSH stimulation). (Book p109)

questions.q: Multinodular goitre etiology is:
questions.exp: MNG: long standing iodine deficiency. (Book p109)

questions.q: A 'dominant nodule' means:
opts: Single palpable nodule + rest of gland palpable
Single palpable nodule + rest not palpable
questions.exp: Dominant nodule: single palpable nodule + rest of gland palpable (isolated nodule: rest not palpable). (Book p109)

questions.q: Risk of malignancy in thyroid swellings: solid swellings have:
opts: Twice the risk of cystic ones
questions.exp: Solid swellings have twice the risk as cystic ones. (Book p109)

questions.q: Regarding malignancy risk in thyroid swellings, males have:
questions.exp: Males have 4 times greater risk than females. (Book p109)

questions.q: A retrosternal goitre is:
questions.exp: Retrosternal goitre: thyroid swelling behind the sternum. (Book p110)

questions.q: The most common type of retrosternal goitre (90%) is:
questions.exp: 2° retrosternal/plunging goitre (m/c, 90%): starts in neck & plunges into mediastinum. (Book p110)

questions.q: 1° mediastinal retrosternal goitre (10%) arises from and is supplied by:
opts: Ectopic thyroid tissue in mediastinum; mediastinal vessels
questions.exp: 1° mediastinal: ectopic thyroid tissue in mediastinum; blood supply mediastinal vessels (2°: neck vessels). (Book p110)

questions.q: The blood supply of a 2° (plunging) retrosternal goitre is from:
questions.exp: 2° retrosternal: neck vessels. (Book p110)

questions.q: On examination of a retrosternal goitre:
questions.exp: Goitre: lower limit not palpable; pressure symptoms dyspnoea/stridor. (Book p110)

questions.q: Pemberton sign: when the patient raises his hands:
opts: Swelling presses on thoracic inlet, blocking venous drainage → facial congestion
questions.exp: Pemberton sign: raise hands → swelling presses on thoracic inlet → blocks venous drainage → facial congestion. (Book p110)

questions.q: The IOC investigation for retrosternal goitre is:
questions.exp: Ix: CECT neck & thorax (IOC); chest x-ray (trachea pushed to opposite side). (Book p110)

questions.q: Most retrosternal goitres are removed via:
questions.exp: Neck/cervical incision & remove goitre: m/c. (Book p110)

questions.q: Median sternotomy is indicated in all EXCEPT:
opts: A primary uncomplicated small plunging goitre
questions.exp: Median sternotomy in: recurrent mediastinal, 1° mediastinal, goitre larger than thoracic inlet, malignant retrosternal goitre. (Book p110)

units.title: Thyroid Embryology & Lingual Thyroid
units.guide: Thyroid descends from foramen caecum (junction anterior 2/3-posterior 1/3 tongue) via thyroglossal tract which obliterates. Lingual thyroid = undescended tissue below tongue (tongue lifted up); FNAC + USG neck to confirm normal gland before excision; thyroxine if it was the only tissue.

units.title: Thyroglossal Cyst: Dx, Mx & Complications
units.sec: Thyroglossal Cyst: Dx, Mx & Complications · p102
units.guide: Persistent tract → subhyoid (m/c) midline swelling moving with deglutition AND tongue protrusion. Sistrunk = cyst + part of hyoid + tract to tongue base; I&D never (fistula). Complications: fistula & PTC in long-standing cases. Vs branchial fistula: lower 1/3 along SCM, congenital/acquired.

units.title: Hyperthyroidism: Features & Causes
units.guide: Thin irritable, weight loss despite appetite, tachycardia, diarrhoea, tremors, heat intolerance, oligomenorrhea. Scan patterns: Graves diffuse ↑ (m/c); Plummer's single hot; toxic nodular goitre multiple hot; factitious & struma ovarii ↓; Jod-Basedow (iodine-induced) ↑; TSH adenoma ↑TSH ↑.

units.title: Antithyroid Drugs & Pre-op Preparation
units.guide: PTU/carbimazole block peroxidase & T4→T3; PTU safe in 1st trimester/lactation; agranulocytosis - sore throat 1st sign. RIA I131 β-rays t½ 7-8 d. Pre-Sx: drugs 6-8 wks to euthyroid, nadolol (long acting) till 7 days post-op (T3 t½), last dose evening before.

units.title: Thyroid Storm
units.guide: Uncontrolled thyrotoxicosis from inadequately prepared patient (m/c), URTI, FNAC, Sx trauma, anaesthetics. Dehydration, hyperthermia, HTN crisis; arrhythmia kills. Mx: aggressive IV fluids (prevent ATN), cold packs, IV steroids + antibiotics, high-dose propranolol, PTU; avoid aspirin.

units.title: Graves: Basics & Eye Signs
units.guide: Autoimmune F>M, m/c hyperthyroid cause; stimulating TRAb (LATS); pretibial myxedema; a/w pernicious anemia & myasthenia. Acropachy = subperiosteal bone. Eye: exophthalmos; von Graefe lid lag + Dalrymple retraction (Muller spasm), Joffroy no forehead wrinkle, Moebius loss of accommodation (severe), Stellwag infrequent blink (mild).

units.title: Graves: Dx & Mx
units.guide: Dx: C/F + autoantibodies; HPE scalloped colloid + tall columnar cells. Mx by status: child drugs; pregnant PTU; adult no goitre drugs→RIA; with goitre drugs→Sx; elderly comorbid drugs→RIA; extensive eye signs drugs→Sx (RIA worsens eyes). Sx: total > subtotal.

units.title: Plummer's & Solitary Toxic Nodule
units.guide: Plummer's/toxic nodular goitre: F:M 5:1, 2nd m/c cause, multiple hot & cold nodules, drugs → total thyroidectomy. Solitary toxic nodule: 5th decade F>M, single hot nodule, drugs → RIA.

units.title: Hypothyroidism: Causes & Features
units.guide: Causes: iodine deficiency (overall m/c), Hashimoto (west m/c), Wolff-Chaikoff (iodine-induced), non-functioning pituitary adenoma ↓TSH (exception), Sheehan (post-partum apoplexy), dyshormonogenesis (TPO deficiency), euthyroid sick syndrome, Refetoff (end-organ T4 resistance). Dull, alopecia, bradycardia, constipation, weight gain, cold intolerance, menorrhagia.

units.title: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis
units.guide: Autoimmune F>M, hereditary, HLA DR3/B8, Down's/Turner's. Blocking receptor + anti-TPO + anti-thyroglobulin antibodies; lymphocytes destroy follicles → hashitoxicosis spike → prolonged hypothyroidism. Long-standing: lymphoma (m/c), FTC, PTC. FNAC lymphocytes + Hurthle; titrate low-dose thyroxine to TSH; total thyroidectomy if goitre.

units.title: Subacute & Post-partum Thyroiditis
units.guide: De Quervain (viral/granulomatous, HLA B35): post-URTI 4-6 wks; painful neck + ↑ESR; hyper→hypo→euthyroid self-limiting (follicles regenerate 2-3 mo); symptomatic + steroids. Post-partum: 2-12 mo (10%), autoimmune 2nd m/c, anti-TPO +, 10-fold Hashimoto risk; correct hypothyroidism.

units.title: Riedel's Thyroiditis & Summary
units.guide: IgG4 fibrosing disease (Peyronie's, Dupuytren's): woody hard painless gland, pressure symptoms; D/D anaplastic; core biopsy; steroids + tamoxifen. Summary table: Hashimoto painless prolonged hypo; De Quervain painful post-URTI spontaneous recovery; Riedel hard gland.

units.title: Goitre: Types & Malignancy Risk
units.guide: Diffuse: iodine deficiency, demand states (pregnancy/puberty), Hashimoto/Graves; untreated → MNG (variable TSH). MNG: long-standing iodine deficiency. Dominant nodule = single palpable + rest palpable. Malignancy risk: solid 2× cystic; males 4× females.

units.title: Retrosternal Goitre
units.guide: Behind sternum; 2° plunging m/c (90%, neck vessels) vs 1° mediastinal (10%, ectopic, mediastinal vessels). Lower limit not palpable; Pemberton sign (arms up → inlet obstruction → facial congestion). CECT neck + thorax IOC; neck incision m/c; sternotomy for recurrent, 1°, larger than inlet, malignant.
